_about: The two sides and their nations (RULES.md §1, §4, §6, §8, §11). Colours come from docs/STYLE.md §2: a side's colour tints the territories it owns (30%); a nation's colour is used for its counters; 'faces' is which way the soldiers on the side's counters face (towards the enemy). 'resources' and 'startWill' are copied from RULES.md (tagged [balanced] there: don't change them here without changing RULES.md). Each resource schedule is a list of {from: 'YYYY-MM', value}; the latest one that has started applies. See docs/DATA.md.

traits.name: Defence in depth
traits.text: Entente attacks on a German box with trench 2+ lose +1 extra step (from Jan 1917, or earlier by research).

traits.name: Strength in numbers at home
traits.text: Germany loses 1 Will per 3 steps lost.

traits.name: Exhaustion
traits.text: All Entente attacks get +1 column (from Aug 1918).

traits.name: No tanks
traits.text: Germany never gets Tank units, unless it researches the A7V (one unit).

start.title: MUTINY
start.text: Whole French divisions refuse to go up to the line. They will hold their trenches, but they will not attack.
start.meaning: French units can’t attack for {turns} months. Then France recovers {willAfter} Will. This happens only once.

end.title: ORDER RESTORED
end.text: The French army has recovered. Leave has been granted and the food is better.
end.meaning: France gains {willAfter} Will and its units can attack again.

traits.name: The 75s
traits.text: German attacks on a French-defended box with trench 0–1 get −1 column (Dec 1914 – Dec 1916).

traits.name: Heavy artillery gap, then production surge
Bleeding
traits.text: Replacements (Manpower) shrink to 2 a month in 1916–17 and 1 in 1918.

traits.name: Supply by sea
traits.text: British units trace supply only to the Channel Ports or Hazebrouck.

traits.name: Holds the Yser
traits.text: Belgium's one unit holds the flooded Yser. It can't attack.

entryTelegram.title: AMERICA ENTERS THE WAR
entryTelegram.text: The United States has declared war on Germany.
entryTelegram.meaning: US Will starts at {will}. The first American troops arrive in {troops}; most come in the summer of 1918.
